stories.title: [Review-driven] Close two HIGH and four MEDIUM/LOW loopholes an independent adversarial review found
stories.description: The review live-fetched Microsoft's own Azure Pipelines docs to check a platform-behavior claim rather than relying on recalled knowledge, and found: (R2, HIGH) the 'Terraform stays include-based, not the anti-pattern' argument was internally inconsistent with its own second example (Markdown-lint) -- Markdown-lint's **.md is a filetype glob (closure: matches anywhere), Terraform's infrastructure/terraform/** was a directory-prefix glob (a new .tf file outside that directory silently never triggered) -- the exact anti-pattern EF-22's own report flagged for Terraform specifically, grouped with .NET's problem, not treated as exempt. (R3, HIGH) the .NET/Node.js exclude list was directory-wide (docs/**, journal/**, .arcane/governance/**), which would ALSO exclude any non-Markdown file a consumer placed in those directories -- a script, manifest, or tooling config -- contradicting ARC-022's unconditional always-trigger list. (R1, MEDIUM) the commit-metadata section implied [skip ci] was opt-in when Azure Pipelines honors it by default (verified live against Microsoft Learn) -- though the actual required-before-merge branch-policy gate is documented as immune to it. (R4, MEDIUM) the 'narrow exclude list' test covered only 3 of ARC-022's 6 named always-trigger categories via ad-hoc substrings, and used an arbitrary length bound as a fake safety proxy. (R5, MEDIUM) block extraction indexed templates by ordinal position, so reordering the doc's sections (or inserting a new template) could silently validate the wrong block with no test failure. (R6, LOW) Terraform/Markdown-lint's asserted pipeline filenames were never declared via a header comment the way .NET's was. A SECOND independent review of the fix (commit a88bd98) verified R1/R3/R5/R6 clean and found two narrower residual gaps in R2/R4: the corrected Terraform filter (**/*.tf, **/*.tfvars) still missed the dependency lock file (.terraform.lock.hcl) and JSON-syntax variants (.tf.json/.tfvars.json) -- none end in .tf/.tfvars, and the lock file specifically is ARC-022's own 'lockfile' category, which is unconditional; and ARC-022 actually names SEVEN always-trigger categories, not six -- 'containers' (DECISIONS.md's ARC-022 entry) was missing from the test's category table, this story's own acceptance criteria and evidence, and architecture.md, consistently, in four places.
acceptanceCriteria: Terraform's include filter is a filetype glob (**/*.tf, **/*.tfvars), not a directory-prefix one
.NET/Node.js exclude list simplified to the single filetype-scoped **/*.md entry
Commit-metadata section states the Azure Pipelines platform default accurately, not as opt-in
Test coverage checks all 7 ARC-022 always-trigger categories, each also nested under a docs-like path
Block extraction is heading-anchored, not ordinal-index-based
Terraform and Markdown-lint YAML blocks gain header comments naming their own file
[Second review round] Terraform include filter also covers .terraform.lock.hcl and .tf.json/.tfvars.json
[Second review round] Always-trigger category count and table corrected from six to seven (containers) everywhere it appears
stories.testEvidence: Rewrote test/cicd-fail-safe-path-filters.test.ts: 18 tests (up from 15), heading-anchored extraction, a 7-category always-trigger table checked both bare and nested under docs/, and a small purpose-scoped glob helper (extension-suffix or exact-literal only -- not a general matcher, since minimatch is only an undeclared transitive dependency here) replacing the ad-hoc substring checks. Full suite (after first review-fix round): 551/552 passing (1 unrelated skip), lint clean, typecheck clean, self-host parity clean. PRD.md's 'Design nuance' section and architecture.md's D1-D3 rewritten to state the corrected principle (glob SHAPE decides safety, not which pipeline it belongs to) rather than leave the superseded, unsound argument on record unmarked. Second review round: added a dedicated test asserting the Terraform include list matches .terraform.lock.hcl (both nested and at repo root) and the two JSON-syntax variants (19 tests total, up from 18); extended the glob helper with a multi-part-extension shape (for .tf.json/.tfvars.json) and an any-depth exact-filename shape (for .terraform.lock.hcl, which isn't an extension pattern); added 'container'/Dockerfile to the always-trigger table (now 7 categories) and corrected every 'six'/'6' mention to seven across this file, architecture.md, and the test file's own comments and test titles. This file's own test verified: 19/19 passing.
